teams.heading: Maro Itoje discusses mental recovery after missing England’s summer Test series
teams.body: England captain Maro Itoje has opened up about his summer absence, admitting he was initially taken aback when Steve Borthwick suggested a break from international duty. After a heavy year personally and professionally, the 31-year-old opted out of the July matches against South Africa, Fiji, and Argentina to prioritise recovery. While he found it "very weird" to watch from afar, Itoje feels the period away was a "wise and prudent decision" to ensure he returns better for the season ahead.

teams.heading: Thomas Ramos linked with sensational move from Toulouse to Racing 92
teams.body: France international Thomas Ramos is reportedly set to depart Toulouse following the 2027 Rugby World Cup. According to reports in L’Equipe, the full-back is being targeted by Top 14 rivals Racing 92 in a move that could see the 29-year-old transition into a fly-half role. Ramos has enjoyed a decorated tenure in the Pink City, securing four league titles and two Investec Champions Cups over the past five years while establishing himself as an ever-present for Les Rouge et Noir.

teams.heading: Ryan Caldwell details his arduous journey from injury to personal peace
teams.body: Former Ireland international Ryan Caldwell has shared a harrowing account of his transition from professional rugby to a life of recovery. The former second-row, who represented Ulster, Bath and Exeter, discusses his struggles with addiction, depression, and the impact of the injuries that cut his career short. Currently living in Belfast, the 41-year-old now works as a meditation and breathwork teacher, a path he details in his forthcoming book, which charts his experience of being broken and successfully rebuilt.

teams.heading: Gonzalo Quesada Banned Under World Rugby’s New Match Official Abuse Process
teams.body: Italy head coach Gonzalo Quesada has been issued a two-Test suspension, becoming the first coach sanctioned under World Rugby’s new Match Official Abuse Sanctioning Process. The ban follows comments made by the Argentine regarding referee Luc Ramos after the loss to the All Blacks. Consequently, Quesada is prohibited from all match-day proceedings—including stadium attendance—for the upcoming fixtures against Australia and the November Test against South Africa. He retains the right to appeal the governing body’s decision.

teams.body: Australia have made nine alterations to their starting XV for the Mendoza rematch, with coach Les Kiss recalling Joseph-Aukuso Suaalii and Ben Donaldson to the run-on side. teams.body: Australia have made 9 changes to their starting side for the second Test against Argentina in Mendoza. teams.body: Japan host Canada at Denka Big Swan Stadium in Niigata City this weekend, celebrating the JRFU’s centenary. Eddie Jones has made five changes to the starting XV that faced Australia, handing a debut to Inoke Burua. Japan will look to break a four-match losing streak against a Canada side currently ranked 24th in the world. Japan have historically dominated this fixture, having not lost to the Canadians in their past 10 meetings, with their last encounter resulting in a 57-15 victory.

teams.heading: Ardie Savea ruled out of fourth Test following shoulder injury
teams.body: The All Blacks must look to salvage a 2-2 series draw without captain Ardie Savea, who has been ruled out of next Saturday’s final Test in Baltimore. Savea sustained a shoulder injury in the 30th minute of Saturday’s 29-24 defeat in Johannesburg. Addressing the setback post-match, head coach Dave Rennie confirmed the skipper will not travel with the squad, though he praised the contribution of replacement Wallace Sititi, insisting the team will not use the captain's absence as an excuse.

teams.heading: South Africa overcome All Blacks at FNB Stadium to lead 2-1
teams.body: The Springboks secured a 29-24 victory over New Zealand on Saturday, moving into a 2-1 series lead with one Test remaining. After trailing in the second half, the world champions relied on their set-piece dominance and a decisive late surge to overcome the visitors in Soweto. However, the win came at a cost, with head coach Rassie Erasmus confirming that Cheslin Kolbe sustained a broken jaw during the match, ruling him out of the final fixture in Baltimore.
